children: US crude oil inventories rose by 1.786 million barrels in the week ending September 18th, following a substantial 7.14 million-barrel increase in the previous week.
Commercial crude oil inventories excluding the SPR have declined by 39 million barrels over the last 23 weeks, but remain nearly 12 million barrels higher for the year.
For the week ending September 18th, another 400,000 barrels left the SPR to support commercial inventories, bringing total SPR holdings to 284.6 million barrels.
The generally accepted operational minimum for SPR holdings is between 250 million and 300 million barrels.
Cushing inventories rose by 2.082 million barrels, after falling by 246,000 barrels in the previous week.
US production remained at 13.944 million bpd in the week ending September 11th, up 462,000 bpd from a year earlier.
Gasoline inventories fell by 2.16 million barrels, while distillate inventories declined by 2.164 million barrels.

title: US Crude Inventories Rise 1.79M Barrels
